# End-to-End Healthcare RCM Services That Maximize Revenue and Minimize Denials

Practolytics offers end-to-end RCM services for healthcare businesses. We make billing easier,
reduce rejected claims, and get you paid faster—so you can focus on patients and improving services.
Our team uses smart tech to handle patient scheduling, insurance eligibility checks, and denial
management services, keeping your cash flow smooth. We help you get more claims approved, cut
delays, and improve healthcare cash flow optimization.
Whether it’s a single clinic or a multi-location healthcare organization, we help you get paid
faster and keep more revenue. Practolytics serves as a trusted revenue cycle management company.
Through healthcare billing compliance, HIPAA-compliant billing, and smooth operations, we adapt to
each payer’s requirements—so your cash flow stays strong.

**Key Benefits**

Faster reimbursements and improved cash flow

Reduced claim denials and billing errors

Expert ICD-10 coding and CPT code billing

Improved days in accounts receivable

Scalable medical billing services for small practices and enterprise groups

[ BOOST YOUR REVENUE ][158]

## What Makes Practolytics the Trusted RCM Partner for 28+ Medical Specialties?

Practolytics serves as a trusted healthcare revenue cycle management partner due to our
specialty-specific expertise, transparent process flows, and measurable financial performances. Our
team helps healthcare providers in over 28 specialties manage their billing and payments. We focus
on what payers need, follow all rules, and help your business run smoothly. Trusted RCM outsourcing
services for any number of specialties.
We understand your specialty language, whether it’s mental health, surgery, urgent care, or
multispecialty. Our expert team manages compliance, payment workflows, charge capture, and entry.

[How We Help][How We Help]

We seamlessly integrate your practice management software with the EHR system to slash admin work
and enhance efficiency. With dedicated managers and real-time analytics, providers attain a complete
view of their revenue performances without compromising quality patient care.

**Why Providers Choose Practolytics**

Specialty-specific billing expertise

Transparent reporting and analytics

Faster onboarding and payer enrollment

Dedicated denial management services

End-to-end revenue leakage prevention

[ TRANSFORM YOUR RCM ][159]

## Why Healthcare Providers Outsource RCM to Practolytics

Healthcare providers choose Practolytics as their outsourced billing services. This lets them focus
on patients while we handle claims, patient payment collections, and denial management services.
Doing billing in-house often leads to delays, errors, and lost revenue. Our tech and experts fix
that—getting clinics paid faster so they can grow without the billing headaches.

[We help you streamline your credentialing process][We help you streamline your credentialing
process]

Our AR follow-up services, claims scrubbing service, remittance advice processing, and accounts
receivable management workflows help providers reduce claim denials and increase collections
efficiency. We also handle value-based care billing, so your practice stays financially ahead. With
our RCM services, providers focus on patients while we take care of coding, claims, insurance
follow-ups, and payment workflows—all done with accuracy and compliance.
**Advantages of Outsourcing RCM**

Lower operational costs and staffing burden

Improved clean claim rate and faster collections

Access to expert coders and billing specialists

Enhanced compliance and audit readiness

Better revenue forecasting and reporting

[ OPTIMIZE YOUR PRACTICE ][160]

[Our Complete Revenue Cycle Management Services][Our Complete Revenue Cycle Management Services]

Streamline your practice’s financial health with our end-to-end RCM solutions. From eligibility
verification and accurate coding to efficient claims management, denial resolution, and patient
billing, we optimize your entire revenue cycle to accelerate cash flow and maximize collections.

### ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][18]
[

### ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][19]
[
['ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ]

### 'ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][20][
[ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ]

### ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][21][
[ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް ]

### ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][22][
[އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ]

### އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][23]

## އެންމެ ހިނގާ

[
1

### އީރާނުން އެމެރިކާގެ ހަމަލާތަކަށް ރައްދުދޭން އާ ގޮތްތަކެއް ރާވައިފި ކަމުގައި އަސްކަރިއްޔާގެ ތަރުޖަމާނު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

ދުނިޔެ|1 ދުވަސް ކުރިން
][24][
2

### އީރާނުގެ މިސައިލްތައް ހުއްޓުވުމުގައި އެމެރިކާގެ ދިފާއީ ނިޒާމުތައް ނުކުޅެދިފައިވާ ކަމަށް ތަޖުރިބާކާރުން ބުނެފި: ރިޕޯޓް

ދުނިޔެ|2 ދުވަސް ކުރިން
][25][
3

### ރައީސް މުއިއްޒުގެ ސަރުކާރުން ތާރުއެޅި މަގު ޕްރޮމޯޓް ކުރުމަށް ސިފައިންގެ މައި މަރުކަޒު ފެންނަ ގޮތަށް ޑްރޯން ފޮޓޯތަކާއި ވީޑިއޯތައް އާއްމުކޮށް ޤައުމު ނުރައްކަލަކަށް ހުށަހަޅައިފި

ރާއްޖެ|19 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][26][
4

### އީރާނުން އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތައް - ތިޔައީ މި ސަރަހައްދުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވި ހުރިހާ ނުބައިކަމެއްގެ އަސްލު، ރެކޯޑު އިތުރަށް ހަޑިކުރާނެ ކަމެއް ނެތް، ހަމަލާތަކުގައި
### ބައިވެރިވާނަމަ ހަމަލާ ދޭނަން!

ދުނިޔެ|18 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][27][
5

### އެމެރިކާގެ ޕެންޓަގަންއަށް އެތައް އަހަރެއް ކުރިން ބޭނުންކުރުން ހުއްޓާލާފައިވާ މުސްކުޅި މިސައިލްތައް ހޯދަން މަޖުބޫރުވީ ކީއްވެ؟

ރިޕޯޓު|12 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][28]

## ރާއްޖެ އެމްވީ ރީލްސް

[
[އިވްނިންގ ޓީ: ކަރަންޓު ބިލު ނުދެއްކިގެން މިއުޅެނީ، އެކަމު އެންމެ ބޮޑު ކަންބޮޑުވުމަކީ ކުޅެން ދާނެ ބޫޓެއް ނެތުން]

އިވްނިންގ ޓީ: ކަރަންޓު ބިލު ނުދެއްކިގެން މިއުޅެނީ، އެކަމު އެންމެ ބޮޑު ކަންބޮޑުވުމަކީ ކުޅެން ދާނެ ބޫޓެއް ނެތުން

[
[ފީފާ ވޯލްޑް ކަޕްގެ ފައިނަލްގައި، އާޖެންޓީނާ އާއި ސްޕެއިން ބައްދަލުކުރި ތާރީޚީ މެޗުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ފޯރިގަދަ ކުޅުމާއެކު، ސަޕޯޓަރުންގެ ފަރާތުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ޖޯޝާއި ފޯރީ]

ފީފާ ވޯލްޑް ކަޕްގެ ފައިނަލްގައި، އާޖެންޓީނާ އާއި ސްޕެއިން ބައްދަލުކުރި ތާރީޚީ މެޗުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ފޯރިގަދަ ކުޅުމާއެކު، ސަޕޯޓަރުންގެ ފަރާތުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ޖޯޝާއި ފޯރީ

[ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް]

## ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް

މިއަހަރުގެ ޖުލައި 16 އާ ހަމައަށް ތަރައްގީގެ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށް ކުރި ހޭދަ މިދިޔަ އަހަރާ އަޅާބަލާއިރު 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށްވެފައިވާއިރު، ބަޖެޓުން މުސާރަ އާއި ޕެންޝަނަށް 8,008.4
މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ހޭދަކޮށްފައިވޭ. ޖުލައި 16 ގެ ނިޔަލަށް ދައުލަތަށް 22.9 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ އާމްދަނީއެއް ލިބުނު ނަމަވެސް، ޚަރަދުތައް މަތިވުމުގެ ސަބަބުން 1.5 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ
ޑެފިސިޓެއް ވަނީ ކުރިމަތިވެފައި. ދައުލަތުން ދޫކޮށްފައިވާ ސެކިއުރިޓީޒްގެ ޖުމްލަ އަދަދު މިހާރު ވަނީ 97.3 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާއަށް އަރާފައި.

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][15]
[
[ރައީސް މުއިއްޒެވެ. ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރު ވެސް ކުޅެވޭނީ އަނގަޔާއި އަތާދިމާވެގެން ނޫން ހެއްޔެވެ؟]

### ރައީސް މުއިއްޒެވެ. ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރު ވެސް ކުޅެވޭނީ އަނގަޔާއި އަތާދިމާވެގެން ނޫން ހެއްޔެވެ؟

## ރާއްޖެ

[
[ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރުކުޅެވޭނެ ފަހި ފުރުޞަތުތައް ހޯދައިދޭން މީގެ ކުރިން ރާއްޖެ ދެކެފައި ނުވާ މިންވަރަށް މިދަނީ ތަރައްގީ ކުރަމުން: ރައީސް މުއިއްޒު]

## ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރުކުޅެވޭނެ ފަހި ފުރުޞަތުތައް ހޯދައިދޭން މީގެ ކުރިން ރާއްޖެ ދެކެފައި ނުވާ މިންވަރަށް މިދަނީ ތަރައްގީ ކުރަމުން: ރައީސް މުއިއްޒު

15 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][46]
[
[ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް]

#### ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][47][
[ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު]

#### ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][48][
[ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް]

#### ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][49][
[ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް ]

#### ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][50]
[
[އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ]

#### އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][51][
[އައްޑޫގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކޮށް ރައްޔިތުންގެ ހައްގުތައް ނިގުޅައިގަނެފި، އެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މުސްތަގްބަލަށް ގޮތް ނިންމާނީ މާލޭ ފިނި ކޮޓަރީގައި ތިބޭ ބައެއް ނޫން: ޝާހިދު]

#### އައްޑޫގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކޮށް ރައްޔިތުންގެ ހައްގުތައް ނިގުޅައިގަނެފި، އެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މުސްތަގްބަލަށް ގޮތް ނިންމާނީ މާލޭ ފިނި ކޮޓަރީގައި ތިބޭ ބައެއް ނޫން: ޝާހިދު

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][52][
[ގޫގުލް އަށް އައްޑޫއިން ދޭން ބުނި ބިމުން ކުލި ނަގާނަން: މޭޔަރު ނިޒާރު]

#### ގޫގުލް އަށް އައްޑޫއިން ދޭން ބުނި ބިމުން ކުލި ނަގާނަން: މޭޔަރު ނިޒާރު

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][53][
[މަސްވެރިކަމުގެ ސިނާއަތް ހީނަރުވީ ކުރީ ސަރުކާރުން ވަޒީފާތައް ބަހާލުމުން ކަމަށް ރައީސް ވިދާޅުވި ނަމަވެސް، މި ސަރުކާރުން އިންތިހާބާ ދިމާކޮށް އެތައް ބަޔަކަށް ވަޒީފާ ދީފައިވޭ!]

#### މަސްވެރިކަމުގެ ސިނާއަތް ހީނަރުވީ ކުރީ ސަރުކާރުން ވަޒީފާތައް ބަހާލުމުން ކަމަށް ރައީސް ވިދާޅުވި ނަމަވެސް، މި ސަރުކާރުން އިންތިހާބާ ދިމާކޮށް އެތައް ބަޔަކަށް ވަޒީފާ ދީފައިވޭ!

12 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][54][
[ކުންފުނިތަކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރާ އާދައިގެ މުވައްޒަފުން ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރަންވާނީ، ދައުލަތުން ކުރާ އިސްރާފާއި އައްޔަންކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ މުވައްޒަފުން މަދުކުރުމަށް ފަހު: ޝަމްހީދު]

#### ކުންފުނިތަކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރާ އާދައިގެ މުވައްޒަފުން ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރަންވާނީ، ދައުލަތުން ކުރާ އިސްރާފާއި އައްޔަންކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ މުވައްޒަފުން މަދުކުރުމަށް ފަހު: ޝަމްހީދު

14 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][55]

## ދުނިޔެ

[
[ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ]

## ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][56]
[
['ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ]

#### 'ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][57][
[އެމެރިކާ އިން ކޯލޭންގް އަށް ދޭ ކޮންމެ ހަމަލާއަކީ ފެށުމުގައިވެސް މަރުވެފައިވާ އަދި ނާކާމިޔާބު އޮޕަރޭޝަނެއް، އެތަނަކީ ފުނޑުފުނޑުކޮށްލެވޭނެ ތަނެއްނޫން: އީރާން]

#### އެމެރިކާ އިން ކޯލޭންގް އަށް ދޭ ކޮންމެ ހަމަލާއަކީ ފެށުމުގައިވެސް މަރުވެފައިވާ އަދި ނާކާމިޔާބު އޮޕަރޭޝަނެއް، އެތަނަކީ ފުނޑުފުނޑުކޮށްލެވޭނެ ތަނެއްނޫން: އީރާން

12 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][58][
[ހޫޘީން ޗައިނާގެ އުޅަނދުފަހަރަށް ހުއްދަ ދެނީ، ބުރާސްފަތިދުވަހު ހުރްމުޒް ހުރަސްކުރީ އެންމެ ޓޭންކަރެއް، އެމެރިކާއާ އީރާނުން ހަމަލާ ބަދަލުކުރަނީ: އެންމެ ފަހުން ހިނގީ ކޮން
ކަމެއް؟]

#### ހޫޘީން ޗައިނާގެ އުޅަނދުފަހަރަށް ހުއްދަ ދެނީ، ބުރާސްފަތިދުވަހު ހުރްމުޒް ހުރަސްކުރީ އެންމެ ޓޭންކަރެއް، އެމެރިކާއާ އީރާނުން ހަމަލާ ބަދަލުކުރަނީ: އެންމެ ފަހުން ހިނގީ ކޮން
#### ކަމެއް؟

13 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][59][
[ހިފާފައިވާ ހުޅަނގު އައްސޭރީގައި އިސްރާއީލު ސިފައިން ބަޑިޖަހާ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހަތަރު މީހަކު ޝަހީދުކޮށްލައިފި]

#### ހިފާފައިވާ ހުޅަނގު އައްސޭރީގައި އިސްރާއީލު ސިފައިން ބަޑިޖަހާ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހަތަރު މީހަކު ޝަހީދުކޮށްލައިފި

13 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][60]
[
[ސޯފާ އަކާ ގުޅޭ މައްސަލަ އެއްގައި ދެކުނު އެފްރިކާގެ ރައީސް މަގާމުން ދުރުކުރުމަށް ޕާލަމަންޓުން ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ އިތުބާރު ނެތްކަމުގެ މައްސަލަ ވަގުތީގޮތުން ހުއްޓާލުމަށް އެ ގައުމުގެ
ކޯޓަކުން އަމުރުކޮށްފި]

#### ސޯފާ އަކާ ގުޅޭ މައްސަލަ އެއްގައި ދެކުނު އެފްރިކާގެ ރައީސް މަގާމުން ދުރުކުރުމަށް ޕާލަމަންޓުން ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ އިތުބާރު ނެތްކަމުގެ މައްސަލަ ވަގުތީގޮތުން ހުއްޓާލުމަށް އެ
#### ގައުމުގެ ކޯޓަކުން އަމުރުކޮށްފި

15 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][61][
[ހަސީނާ އެނބުރިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވުމާއެކު ކުރިމަތިވި ފިއްތުންތަކާއެކު ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ރައީސް މުޙައްމަދު ޝަހާބުއްދީން އިސްތިއުފާ ދެއްވަން ނިންމަވައިފި]

#### ހަސީނާ އެނބުރިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވުމާއެކު ކުރިމަތިވި ފިއްތުންތަކާއެކު ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ރައީސް މުޙައްމަދު ޝަހާބުއްދީން އިސްތިއުފާ ދެއްވަން ނިންމަވައިފި

16 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][62][

#### ބަހްރައިންއާއި އުރުދުންގައި ހުންނަ އެމެރިކާގެ މުހިންމު ދެ އަސްކަރީ މަރުކަޒަކަށް އީރާނުގެ އަސްކަރިއްޔާއިން ހަމަލާދީފި

17 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][63][
[އިރާގުގެ ބޮޑުވަޒީރު މެދުވެރިކޮށް އެމެރިކާއިން ހުށަހެޅި ހަނގުރާމަ ހުއްޓާލުމުގެ ހުށަހެޅުމަށް އީރާނުން ނޫނެކޭ ބުނެފި]

#### އިރާގުގެ ބޮޑުވަޒީރު މެދުވެރިކޮށް އެމެރިކާއިން ހުށަހެޅި ހަނގުރާމަ ހުއްޓާލުމުގެ ހުށަހެޅުމަށް އީރާނުން ނޫނެކޭ ބުނެފި

17 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][64][
[އީރާނުން އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތައް - ތިޔައީ މި ސަރަހައްދުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވި ހުރިހާ ނުބައިކަމެއްގެ އަސްލު، ރެކޯޑު އިތުރަށް ހަޑިކުރާނެ ކަމެއް ނެތް، ހަމަލާތަކުގައި ބައިވެރިވާނަމަ
ހަމަލާ ދޭނަން!]

#### އީރާނުން އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތައް - ތިޔައީ މި ސަރަހައްދުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވި ހުރިހާ ނު

[ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް]

## ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް

މިއަހަރުގެ ޖުލައި 16 އާ ހަމައަށް ތަރައްގީގެ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށް ކުރި ހޭދަ މިދިޔަ އަހަރާ އަޅާބަލާއިރު 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށްވެފައިވާއިރު، ބަޖެޓުން މުސާރަ އާއި ޕެންޝަނަށް 8,008.4
މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ހޭދަކޮށްފައިވޭ. ޖުލައި 16 ގެ ނިޔަލަށް ދައުލަތަށް 22.9 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ އާމްދަނީއެއް ލިބުނު ނަމަވެސް، ޚަރަދުތައް މަތިވުމުގެ ސަބަބުން 1.5 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ
ޑެފިސިޓެއް ވަނީ ކުރިމަތިވެފައި. ދައުލަތުން ދޫކޮށްފައިވާ ސެކިއުރިޓީޒްގެ ޖުމްލަ އަދަދު މިހާރު ވަނީ 97.3 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާއަށް އަރާފައި.

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][15]
[
[ރައީސް މުއިއްޒެވެ. ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރު ވެސް ކުޅެވޭނީ އަނގަޔާއި އަތާދިމާވެގެން ނޫން ހެއްޔެވެ؟]

### ރައީސް މުއިއްޒެވެ. ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރު ވެސް ކުޅެވޭނީ އަނގަޔާއި އަތާދިމާވެގެން ނޫން ހެއްޔެވެ؟

8 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][16]
[

### އިވްނިންގ ޓީ: ކަރަންޓު ބިލު ނުދެއްކިގެން މިއުޅެނީ، އެކަމު އެންމެ ބޮޑު ކަންބޮޑުވުމަކީ ކުޅެން ދާނެ ބޫޓެއް ނެތުން

8 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][17]
[

### ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][18]
[

### ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][19]
[
['ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ]

### 'ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][20][
[ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ]

### ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][21][
[ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް ]

### ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][22][
[އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ]

### އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][23]

## އެންމެ ހިނގާ

[
1

### އީރާނުން އެމެރިކާގެ ހަމަލާތަކަށް ރައްދުދޭން އާ ގޮތްތަކެއް ރާވައިފި ކަމުގައި އަސްކަރިއްޔާގެ ތަރުޖަމާނު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

ދުނިޔެ|1 ދުވަސް ކުރިން
][24][
2

### އީރާނުގެ މިސައިލްތައް ހުއްޓުވުމުގައި އެމެރިކާގެ ދިފާއީ ނިޒާމުތައް ނުކުޅެދިފައިވާ ކަމަށް ތަޖުރިބާކާރުން ބުނެފި: ރިޕޯޓް

ދުނިޔެ|2 ދުވަސް ކުރިން
][25][
3

### ރައީސް މުއިއްޒުގެ ސަރުކާރުން ތާރުއެޅި މަގު ޕްރޮމޯޓް ކުރުމަށް ސިފައިންގެ މައި މަރުކަޒު ފެންނަ ގޮތަށް ޑްރޯން ފޮޓޯތަކާއި ވީޑިއޯތައް އާއްމުކޮށް ޤައުމު ނުރައްކަލަކަށް ހުށަހަޅައިފި

ރާއްޖެ|19 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][26][
4

### އީރާނުން އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތައް - ތިޔައީ މި ސަރަހައްދުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވި ހުރިހާ ނުބައިކަމެއްގެ އަސްލު، ރެކޯޑު އިތުރަށް ހަޑިކުރާނެ ކަމެއް ނެތް، ހަމަލާތަކުގައި
### ބައިވެރިވާނަމަ ހަމަލާ ދޭނަން!

ދުނިޔެ|18 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][27][
5

### އެމެރިކާގެ ޕެންޓަގަންއަށް އެތައް އަހަރެއް ކުރިން ބޭނުންކުރުން ހުއްޓާލާފައިވާ މުސްކުޅި މިސައިލްތައް ހޯދަން މަޖުބޫރުވީ ކީއްވެ؟

ރިޕޯޓު|12 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][28]

## ރާއްޖެ އެމްވީ ރީލްސް

[
[އިވްނިންގ ޓީ: ކަރަންޓު ބިލު ނުދެއްކިގެން މިއުޅެނީ، އެކަމު އެންމެ ބޮޑު ކަންބޮޑުވުމަކީ ކުޅެން ދާނެ ބޫޓެއް ނެތުން]

އިވްނިންގ ޓީ: ކަރަންޓު ބިލު ނުދެއްކިގެން މިއުޅެނީ، އެކަމު އެންމެ ބޮޑު ކަންބޮޑުވުމަކީ ކުޅެން ދާނެ ބޫޓެއް ނެތުން

[
[ފީފާ ވޯލްޑް ކަޕްގެ ފައިނަލްގައި، އާޖެންޓީނާ އާއި ސްޕެއިން ބައްދަލުކުރި ތާރީޚީ މެޗުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ފޯރިގަދަ ކުޅުމާއެކު، ސަޕޯޓަރުންގެ ފަރާތުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ޖޯޝާއި ފޯރީ]

ފީފާ ވޯލްޑް ކަޕްގެ ފައިނަލްގައި، އާޖެންޓީނާ އާއި ސްޕެއިން ބައްދަލުކުރި ތާރީޚީ މެޗުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ފޯރިގަދަ ކުޅުމާއެކު، ސަޕޯޓަރުންގެ ފަރާތުން ފެނިގެންދިޔަ ޖޯޝާއި ފޯރީ

[ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް]

## ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް

މިއަހަރުގެ ޖުލައި 16 އާ ހަމައަށް ތަރައްގީގެ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށް ކުރި ހޭދަ މިދިޔަ އަހަރާ އަޅާބަލާއިރު 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށްވެފައިވާއިރު، ބަޖެޓުން މުސާރަ އާއި ޕެންޝަނަށް 8,008.4
މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ހޭދަކޮށްފައިވޭ. ޖުލައި 16 ގެ ނިޔަލަށް ދައުލަތަށް 22.9 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ އާމްދަނީއެއް ލިބުނު ނަމަވެސް، ޚަރަދުތައް މަތިވުމުގެ ސަބަބުން 1.5 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާގެ
ޑެފިސިޓެއް ވަނީ ކުރިމަތިވެފައި. ދައުލަތުން ދޫކޮށްފައިވާ ސެކިއުރިޓީޒްގެ ޖުމްލަ އަދަދު މިހާރު ވަނީ 97.3 ބިލިއަން ރުފިޔާއަށް އަރާފައި.

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][15]
[
[ރައީސް މުއިއްޒެވެ. ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރު ވެސް ކުޅެވޭނީ އަނގަޔާއި އަތާދިމާވެގެން ނޫން ހެއްޔެވެ؟]

### ރައީސް މުއިއްޒެވެ. ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރު ވެސް ކުޅެވޭނީ އަނގަޔާއި އަތާދިމާވެގެން ނޫން ހެއްޔެވެ؟

8 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][16]
[

### އިވްނިންގ ޓީ: ކަރަންޓު ބިލު ނުދެއްކިގެން މިއުޅެނީ، އެކަމު އެންމެ ބޮޑު ކަންބޮޑުވުމަކީ ކުޅެން ދާނެ ބޫޓެއް ނެތުން

8 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][17]
[

### ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][18]
[

### ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][19]
[
['ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ]

### 'ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][20][
[ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ]

## ރާއްޖެ

[
[ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރުކުޅެވޭނެ ފަހި ފުރުޞަތުތައް ހޯދައިދޭން މީގެ ކުރިން ރާއްޖެ ދެކެފައި ނުވާ މިންވަރަށް މިދަނީ ތަރައްގީ ކުރަމުން: ރައީސް މުއިއްޒު]

## ޒުވާނުންނަށް ކުޅިވަރުކުޅެވޭނެ ފަހި ފުރުޞަތުތައް ހޯދައިދޭން މީގެ ކުރިން ރާއްޖެ ދެކެފައި ނުވާ މިންވަރަށް މިދަނީ ތަރައްގީ ކުރަމުން: ރައީސް މުއިއްޒު

15 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][46]
[
[ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް]

#### ބަޖެޓު ޚަރަދުގެ 87 އިންސައްތަ ހިންގުމަށް، ޕީއެސްއައިޕީ މަޝްރޫއުތަކަށްކުރި ހޭދަ 16 އިންސައްތަ ދަށަށް، ބަޖެޓް ޑެފިސިޓް 1.5 ބިލިއަނަށް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][47][
[ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު]

#### ސަވާހެލި އައްޑޫގެ އިހުތިސާސުން ސަރުކާރުން ވަކިކުރީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ޓޫރިޒަމް ތަރައްގީވިޔަ ނުދޭން: ފައްޔާޒު

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][48][
[ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް]

#### ރާއްޖޭގެ އަތޮޅުތަކުން ކުރިއެރުން ލިބެން އޮތީ ސަރުކާރުން ކޮންމެ ކަމަކަށް ވަނުމުގެ ބަދަލުގައި، ކަންކަން ކުރެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހޯދައިދީ، މަރުކަޒީ ބާރުތައް ދޫކޮށްލައިގެން: ފައިސަލް

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][49][
[ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް ]

#### ޝިއާއުގެ މަރު: ޝާހިލްއަށް އިއްވި 3 އަހަރުގެ ހުކުމް އަނެއްކާ ވެސް އިސްތިއުނާފު ކުރުމަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުން މިފަހަރު ވެސް ބަލައިނުގަތް

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][50]
[
[އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ]

#### އައްޑޫ ސިޓީގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކުރުމަކީ އެ ސިޓީގެ ތަރައްގީއަށް ހުރަސްއެޅުމަށް ހިންގާފައިވާ ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލެއް: އެމްޑީޕީ

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][51][
[އައްޑޫގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކޮށް ރައްޔިތުންގެ ހައްގުތައް ނިގުޅައިގަނެފި، އެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މުސްތަގްބަލަށް ގޮތް ނިންމާނީ މާލޭ ފިނި ކޮޓަރީގައި ތިބޭ ބައެއް ނޫން: ޝާހިދު]

#### އައްޑޫގެ އިހްތިސާސުން ސަވާހިލި ވަކިކޮށް ރައްޔިތުންގެ ހައްގުތައް ނިގުޅައިގަނެފި، އެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މުސްތަގްބަލަށް ގޮތް ނިންމާނީ މާލޭ ފިނި ކޮޓަރީގައި ތިބޭ ބައެއް ނޫން: ޝާހިދު

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][52][
[ގޫގުލް އަށް އައްޑޫއިން ދޭން ބުނި ބިމުން ކުލި ނަގާނަން: މޭޔަރު ނިޒާރު]

#### ގޫގުލް އަށް އައްޑޫއިން ދޭން ބުނި ބިމުން ކުލި ނަގާނަން: މޭޔަރު ނިޒާރު

11 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][53][
[މަސްވެރިކަމުގެ ސިނާއަތް ހީނަރުވީ ކުރީ ސަރުކާރުން ވަޒީފާތައް ބަހާލުމުން ކަމަށް ރައީސް ވިދާޅުވި ނަމަވެސް، މި ސަރުކާރުން އިންތިހާބާ ދިމާކޮށް އެތައް ބަޔަކަށް ވަޒީފާ ދީފައިވޭ!]

#### މަސްވެރިކަމުގެ ސިނާއަތް ހީނަރުވީ ކުރީ ސަރުކާރުން ވަޒީފާތައް ބަހާލުމުން ކަމަށް ރައީސް ވިދާޅުވި ނަމަވެސް، މި ސަރުކާރުން އިންތިހާބާ ދިމާކޮށް އެތައް ބަޔަކަށް ވަޒީފާ ދީފައިވޭ!

12 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][54][
[ކުންފުނިތަކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރާ އާދައިގެ މުވައްޒަފުން ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރަންވާނީ، ދައުލަތުން ކުރާ އިސްރާފާއި އައްޔަންކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ މުވައްޒަފުން މަދުކުރުމަށް ފަހު: ޝަމްހީދު]

#### ކުންފުނިތަކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރާ އާދައިގެ މުވައްޒަފުން ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރަންވާނީ، ދައުލަތުން ކުރާ އިސްރާފާއި އައްޔަންކޮށްފައިވާ ސިޔާސީ މުވައްޒަފުން މަދުކުރުމަށް ފަހު: ޝަމްހީދު

14 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][55]

## ދުނިޔެ

[
[ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ]

## ސެޓެލައިޓް މެދުވެރިކޮށް ނަގާ ގަލްފް ސަރަހައްދުގެ ފޮޓޯތައް އާންމުކުރުން ފަސްކޮށްދިނުމަށް އެމެރިކާއިން އެދިފައިވާ އެދުމަށް އީޔޫ އިން އެއްބަސްވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][56]
[
['ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ]

#### 'ސާފު އުސޫލެއް': މަރުވާ އީރާނުގެ ކޮންމެ މަދަނީ ރައްޔިތެއްގެ ބަދަލުގައި އެމެރިކާ ސިފައިންގެ މީހަކު މަރާލާނެ ކަމަށް އީރާނުގެ އިސް ކޮމާންޑަރަކު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

10 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][57][
[އެމެރިކާ އިން ކޯލޭންގް އަށް ދޭ ކޮންމެ ހަމަލާއަކީ ފެށުމުގައިވެސް މަރުވެފައިވާ އަދި ނާކާމިޔާބު އޮޕަރޭޝަނެއް، އެތަނަކީ ފުނޑުފުނޑުކޮށްލެވޭނެ ތަނެއްނޫން: އީރާން]

#### އެމެރިކާ އިން ކޯލޭންގް އަށް ދޭ ކޮންމެ ހަމަލާއަކީ ފެށުމުގައިވެސް މަރުވެފައިވާ އަދި ނާކާމިޔާބު އޮޕަރޭޝަނެއް، އެތަނަކީ ފުނޑުފުނޑުކޮށްލެވޭނެ ތަނެއްނޫން: އީރާން

12 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][58][
[ހޫޘީން ޗައިނާގެ އުޅަނދުފަހަރަށް ހުއްދަ ދެނީ، ބުރާސްފަތިދުވަހު ހުރްމުޒް ހުރަސްކުރީ އެންމެ ޓޭންކަރެއް، އެމެރިކާއާ އީރާނުން ހަމަލާ ބަދަލުކުރަނީ: އެންމެ ފަހުން ހިނގީ ކޮން
ކަމެއް؟]

#### ހޫޘީން ޗައިނާގެ އުޅަނދުފަހަރަށް ހުއްދަ ދެނީ، ބުރާސްފަތިދުވަހު ހުރްމުޒް ހުރަސްކުރީ އެންމެ ޓޭންކަރެއް، އެމެރިކާއާ އީރާނުން ހަމަލާ ބަދަލުކުރަނީ: އެންމެ ފަހުން ހިނގީ ކޮން
#### ކަމެއް؟

13 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][59][
[ހިފާފައިވާ ހުޅަނގު އައްސޭރީގައި އިސްރާއީލު ސިފައިން ބަޑިޖަހާ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހަތަރު މީހަކު ޝަހީދުކޮށްލައިފި]

#### ހިފާފައިވާ ހުޅަނގު އައްސޭރީގައި އިސްރާއީލު ސިފައިން ބަޑިޖަހާ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހަތަރު މީހަކު ޝަހީދުކޮށްލައިފި

13 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން
][60]
[
[ސޯފާ އަކާ ގުޅޭ މައްސަލަ އެއްގައި ދެކުނު އެފްރިކާގެ ރައީސް މަގާމުން ދުރުކުރުމަށް ޕާލަމަންޓުން ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ އިތުބާރު ނެތްކަމުގެ މައްސަލަ ވަގުތީގޮތުން ހުއްޓާލުމަށް އެ ގައުމުގެ
ކޯޓަކުން އަމުރުކޮށްފި]

#### ސޯފާ އަކާ ގުޅޭ މައްސަލަ އެއްގައި ދެކުނު އެފްރިކާގެ ރައީސް މަގާމުން ދުރުކުރުމަށް ޕާލަމަންޓުން ކުރިއަށްގެންދާ އިތުބާރު ނެތްކަމުގެ މައްސަލަ ވަގުތީގޮތުން ހުއްޓާލުމަށް އެ
#### ގައުމުގެ ކޯޓަކުން އަމުރުކޮށްފި

15 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][61][
[ހަސީނާ އެނބުރިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވުމާއެކު ކުރިމަތިވި ފިއްތުންތަކާއެކު ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ރައީސް މުޙައްމަދު ޝަހާބުއްދީން އިސްތިއުފާ ދެއްވަން ނިންމަވައިފި]

#### ހަސީނާ އެނބުރިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވުމާއެކު ކުރިމަތިވި ފިއްތުންތަކާއެކު ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ރައީސް މުޙައްމަދު ޝަހާބުއްދީން އިސްތިއުފާ ދެއްވަން ނިންމަވައިފި

16 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][62][

#### ބަހްރައިންއާއި އުރުދުންގައި ހުންނަ އެމެރިކާގެ މުހިންމު ދެ އަސްކަރީ މަރުކަޒަކަށް އީރާނުގެ އަސްކަރިއްޔާއިން ހަމަލާދީފި

17 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][63][
[އިރާގުގެ ބޮޑުވަޒީރު މެދުވެރިކޮށް އެމެރިކާއިން ހުށަހެޅި ހަނގުރާމަ ހުއްޓާލުމުގެ ހުށަހެޅުމަށް އީރާނުން ނޫނެކޭ ބުނެފި]

#### އިރާގުގެ ބޮޑުވަޒީރު މެދުވެރިކޮށް އެމެރިކާއިން ހުށަހެޅި ހަނގުރާމަ ހުއްޓާލުމުގެ ހުށަހެޅުމަށް އީރާނުން ނޫނެކޭ ބުނެފި

17 ގަޑިއިރު ކުރިން][64][
[އީރާނުން އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތައް - ތިޔައީ މި ސަރަހައްދުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވި ހުރިހާ ނުބައިކަމެއްގެ އަސްލު، ރެކޯޑު އިތުރަށް ހަޑިކުރާނެ ކަމެއް ނެތް، ހަމަލާތަކުގައި ބައިވެރިވާނަމަ
ހަމަލާ ދޭނަން!]

#### އީރާނުން އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތައް - ތިޔައީ މި ސަރަހައްދުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވި ހުރިހާ ނު

# INDIA'S LEADING STEM CELL BANK AND THERAPY RESEARCH CENTER

Stem Cell Banking and Research is our forte. With the technological know-how and expertise of
banking from 10 different sources, ReeLabs is India's first and only bank with the capabilities to
offer Amniotic Sac, Amniotic Fluid and Placental Stem Cell Banking facility along with Cord Blood
and Cord Tissue. Our commitment to stem cells has successfully helped over 1,00,000 people from all
walks of life. Our tie-ups with over 300 hospitals, medical centres and specialty clinics across
India help us to be there for you whenever and wherever you need us. Using state of the art
technology, we ensure the highest count and viability of cells, so that they can be effectively used
for treatment, when required.


You can get in touch with us by filling out the [contact form][37], or by giving us a call on our
Toll Free no: 1800-222-454 (Mon-Fri, 10am-6pm).
 

OUR SERVICES

[Learn why celebrities bank with us][38]

### STEM CELL BANKING FROM 10 SOURCES

Banking from 10 different sources and the only company in India to have the capabilities to bank
stem cells from the Amniotic Sac, Amniotic Fluid and Placenta.

[Read More][39]
[Banking-main1.jpg]
[Treatment-main1.jpg]

### ADVANCED STEM CELL THERAPY

From Leukaemia to Thalassemia, Stem Cell Therapy is the first line of treatment for over 80 approved
disorders.

[Read More][40]

### WHY CHOOSE REELABS

We have devoted the past decade to establishing ReeLabs as a recognised authority in the field of
stem cells. Using our proprietary technology, stem cells are processed to ensure they possess the
best features.

[Read More][41]
[OurStory-Home2.jpg]
[Facility-main.jpg]

## OUR FACILITY

ASIA'S LARGEST STEM CELL FACILITY

In its continued commitment to stem cell research, ReeLabs has set up Asia's largest, state of the
art stem cell facility in the heart of Mumbai.

* Flood proof location.
* Earthquake resistant construction.
* Specially designed for stem cell banking and research.

[Know More][42]

## REELABS IN NUMBERS

13

PATENTS

7

CLINICAL TRIALS

20

PROPRIETARY INVENTIONS

300+

INTERNATIONAL PUBLICATIONS

## RECOGNITION

### INDIA'S BEST ENTERPRISE FOR INNOVATION IN STEM CELLS

ReeLabs Pvt. Ltd. has been awarded India's Best Enterprise For Innovation in Stem Cells, Cellular
Medicine and Regenerative Medicine - organized by Navabharat Times in Mumbai on 5th of September
2023.

 

The award was presented by the Honorable Union Health Minister Dr. Bharti Pawar.

[ReeLabs winning the Navabharat Award for India's Best Enterprise For Innovation in Stem Cells and
Cellular Medicine]

Hiral Thanawala

> “Thank you, for your professionalism, expertise and commitment to providing top-notch services."

Jyotsna Patil

> "I would like to highly recommend their service and this company for stem cell preservation."

Mehul Nisar

> “They are the best in the industry in terms of offerings, benefits and customer service."

Mansi Goel

> "Staff is active, co-operated and helpful. I liked the service and would recommend my friends."

> “Extremely impressed with the precise and thorough directions and assistance given”

INDIA'S BEST
STEM CELL
BANK

[Learn more ][36]

# INDIA'S LEADING STEM CELL BANK AND THERAPY RESEARCH CENTER

Stem Cell Banking and Research is our forte. With the technological know-how and expertise of
banking from 10 different sources, ReeLabs is India's first and only bank with the capabilities to
offer Amniotic Sac, Amniotic Fluid and Placental Stem Cell Banking facility along with Cord Blood
and Cord Tissue. Our commitment to stem cells has successfully helped over 1,00,000 people from all
walks of life. Our tie-ups with over 300 hospitals, medical centres and specialty clinics across
India help us to be there for you whenever and wherever you need us. Using state of the art
technology, we ensure the highest count and viability of cells, so that they can be effectively used
for treatment, when required.


You can get in touch with us by filling out the [contact form][37], or by giving us a call on our
Toll Free no: 1800-222-454 (Mon-Fri, 10am-6pm).
 

OUR SERVICES

[Learn why celebrities bank with us][38]

### STEM CELL BANKING FROM 10 SOURCES

Banking from 10 different sources and the only company in India to have the capabilities to bank
stem cells from the Amniotic Sac, Amniotic Fluid and Placenta.

[Read More][39]
[Banking-main1.jpg]
[Treatment-main1.jpg]

### ADVANCED STEM CELL THERAPY

From Leukaemia to Thalassemia, Stem Cell Therapy is the first line of treatment for over 80 approved
disorders.

[Read More][40]

### WHY CHOOSE REELABS

We have devoted the past decade to establishing ReeLabs as a recognised authority in the field of
stem cells. Using our proprietary technology, stem cells are processed to ensure they possess the
best features.

[Read More][41]
[OurStory-Home2.jpg]
[Facility-main.jpg]

## OUR FACILITY

ASIA'S LARGEST STEM CELL FACILITY

In its continued commitment to stem cell research, ReeLabs has set up Asia's largest, state of the
art stem cell facility in the heart of Mumbai.

* Flood proof location.
* Earthquake resistant construction.
* Specially designed for stem cell banking and research.

[Know More][42]

## REELABS IN NUMBERS

13

PATENTS

7

CLINICAL TRIALS

20

PROPRIETARY INVENTIONS

300+

INTERNATIONAL PUBLICATIONS

## RECOGNITION

### INDIA'S BEST ENTERPRISE FOR INNOVATION IN STEM CELLS

ReeLabs Pvt. Ltd. has been awarded India's Best Enterprise For Innovation in Stem Cells, Cellular
Medicine and Regenerative Medicine - organized by Navabharat Times in Mumbai on 5th of September
2023.

 

The award was presented by the Honorable Union Health Minister Dr. Bharti Pawar.

[ReeLabs winning the Navabharat Award for India's Best Enterprise For Innovation in Stem Cells and
Cellular Medicine]

Hiral Thanawala

> “Thank you, for your professionalism, expertise and commitment to providing top-notch services."

Jyotsna Patil

> "I would like to highly recommend their service and this company for stem cell preservation."

Mehul Nisar

> “Their team and service is very prompt. Their nurse in the hospital also was also very helpful.”

Aarti Kalera

> “They are the best in the industry in terms of offerings, benefits and customer service."

Mansi Goel

> "Staff is active, co-operated and helpful. I liked the service and would recommend my friends."

Rohini Vakil Kapoor

> “Extremely impressed with the precise and thorough directions and assistance given”

A Radically Improved Bone Marrow Harvest System

[Explore][20]

# MARROWMINER

# RegenMed Systems has developed a revolutionary FDA-approved, rapid, minimally-invasive, and
# clinically-proven system for harvesting bone marrow from a single puncture under local anesthesia.
#  

[MarrowMiner_photofixed.jpg]
 

# Marrowminer is the first significant improvement in bone marrow harvesting in the last 50 years.

[MMFeatures1-01.jpg]

# Results Published in Leading Bone Marrow Journal

[The MarrowMiner: A Novel Minimally Invasive and Effective Device for the Harvest of Bone Marrow.
Published in the Biology of Blood & Marrow Transplantation (BBMT), Online. September 2019.
In-Press.]

[The MarrowMiner: A Novel Minimally Invasive and Effective Device for the Harvest of Bone
Marrow.][21] Published in the Biology of Blood & Marrow Transplantation (BBMT), Online. September
2019. In-Press.

# Setting a new standard for bone marrow collection.

## **HIGHER QUALITY**

Greater yield of clinically-proven, vital stem cell subtypes

## **FASTER**

Harvest potent cells in only 10-20min (4-10x faster than traditional means)

## **MINIMALLY INVASIVE**

Only one bone puncture required, can be performed with local anesthesia

## **COST-EFFECTIVE**

Inexpensive harvesting, without lengthy OR collection

[MMFeatures5-05.jpg]

##  

## **ENHANCES RESEARCH: **

## Higher-numbers of stem & progenitor cells, and a more consistent harvest for autologous and
## allogeneic marrow use.

##  

## **ENABLES PROCEDURES UTILIZING BONE MARROW: **

## Facilitates improved bone marrow transplantation and a widening array of applications using
## marrow-derived cells.

 

[MMFeatures4_blueonly-04.jpg]

The MarrowMiner has the potential to improve clinical outcomes
and reduce cost simultaneously.

[ Simply a better way to harvest bone marrow. ][22]

RegenMed Systems

**Introducing the MARROWMINER**

A Radically Improved Bone Marrow Harvest System

[Explore][20]

# MARROWMINER

# RegenMed Systems has developed a revolutionary FDA-approved, rapid, minimally-invasive, and
# clinically-proven system for harvesting bone marrow from a single puncture under local anesthesia.
#  

[MarrowMiner_photofixed.jpg]
 

# Marrowminer is the first significant improvement in bone marrow harvesting in the last 50 years.

[MMFeatures1-01.jpg]

# Results Published in Leading Bone Marrow Journal

[The MarrowMiner: A Novel Minimally Invasive and Effective Device for the Harvest of Bone Marrow.
Published in the Biology of Blood & Marrow Transplantation (BBMT), Online. September 2019.
In-Press.]

[The MarrowMiner: A Novel Minimally Invasive and Effective Device for the Harvest of Bone
Marrow.][21] Published in the Biology of Blood & Marrow Transplantation (BBMT), Online. September
2019. In-Press.

# Setting a new standard for bone marrow collection.

## **HIGHER QUALITY**

Greater yield of clinically-proven, vital stem cell subtypes

## **FASTER**

Harvest potent cells in only 10-20min (4-10x faster than traditional means)

## **MINIMALLY INVASIVE**

Only one bone puncture required, can be performed with local anesthesia

## **COST-EFFECTIVE**

Inexpensive harvesting, without lengthy OR collection

[MMFeatures5-05.jpg]

##  

## **ENHANCES RESEARCH: **

## Higher-numbers of stem & progenitor cells, and a more consistent harvest for autologous and
## allogeneic marrow use.

##  

## **ENABLES PROCEDURES UTILIZING BONE MARROW: **

## Facilitates improved bone marrow transplantation and a widening array of applications using
## marrow-derived cells.

 

[MMFeatures4_blueonly-04.jpg]

The MarrowMiner has the potential to improve clinical outcomes
and reduce cost simultaneously.

[ Simply a better way to harvest bone marrow. ][22]

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

What is the Natural History of a Disease?

The Natural History of a Disease is the typical progression of the disease over a person’s lifetime
starting from its onset

What is the purpose of a Natural History Study?

Natural History studies are observational studies that gather comprehensive data on the course of
the disease to gain a better understanding of its progression and impact on patients. Data captured
may include information on the physical signs and symptoms patients experience, test results (for
example blood tests or imaging), genetic information, and health-related quality of life, over a
period of time. This information helps describe the disease course and identify important factors
(e.g. demographic, genetic, and/or lab test results), that may contribute to better or worse disease
outcomes.

What compensation is provided when participating in a Natural History Study?

Travel, accommodation, and food stipend would be provided. Study assessments are provided free of
charge.

What are the benefits of participating?

Natural History Studies are particularly important for rare diseases. Given the diversity of
symptoms and the small size of the patient population, these studies are often the only opportunity
for researchers and physicians to address significant knowledge gaps and obtain a robust
understanding of the disease and patient experience.

Engaging in a Natural History Study offers numerous benefits to the community, such as:
* Raising awareness in medical, academic and pharmaceutical sectors
* Empowering rare disease patient communities with knowledge and support for advocating better
  healthcare policies and support services
* Enhancing patient care with improved insights into disease progression, allowing for more
  personalized treatment plans and potentially earlier detection of complications
* Contributing to advancements in healthcare

How do Natural History Studies help inform and design clinical trials?

These studies provide various avenues to help inform and design clinical trials, such as:
* Highlighting areas of unmet medical need
* Understanding characteristics of the patient population to define a treatment benefit from a
  patient’s perspective.
* Describing disease progression, enabling the identification of clinical outcome measures and
  biomarkers
* Provide patient-centric data for health authorities such as the FDA, and other public health
  institutions to use in their review processes of investigational treatments.

## Mission, Vision & Values

Our mission is to seek gene therapy cures for patients with devastating rare diseases through the
most innovative science and platforms to fulfill the promise of gene therapy for the betterment of
our industry, science and humanity.

Trust is given and trust is earned – it’s a balance. The word “trust” comes from the
“Proto-Indo-European word “deru” which means “to be firm, solid, steadfast.” Trust is the ground and
foundation for everything we do.

### Generosity

+
Being generous means following up, sharing our best ideas, forgiving ourselves and others, asking
who needs us, treating our word as gold, taking time to truly see others, and so many other things.
The word “generous” has the same root as the word “gene” – which means “to beget.” Genes thrive on
the generosity of others. What more is there to say?

### Curiosity

+
The wonder of a child staring up at the night sky. Humility, selflessness. No single one of us can
do this job alone and it is ok to ask for help. Curiosity is derived from the Latin word, “cura”
which gave birth to the word “care” as well as “cure.” Generosity is to curiosity what gene is to
cure.

### Elevate

+
Derived from the Latin word “levis,” which means “light” as opposed to heavy. How can we bring
trust, generosity and curiosity to elevate ourselves, each other, the pipeline and ultimately the
life experience of patients and their families?

starting from its onset

What is the purpose of a Natural History Study?

Natural History studies are observational studies that gather comprehensive data on the course of
the disease to gain a better understanding of its progression and impact on patients. Data captured
may include information on the physical signs and symptoms patients experience, test results (for
example blood tests or imaging), genetic information, and health-related quality of life, over a
period of time. This information helps describe the disease course and identify important factors
(e.g. demographic, genetic, and/or lab test results), that may contribute to better or worse disease
outcomes.

What compensation is provided when participating in a Natural History Study?

Travel, accommodation, and food stipend would be provided. Study assessments are provided free of
charge.

What are the benefits of participating?

Natural History Studies are particularly important for rare diseases. Given the diversity of
symptoms and the small size of the patient population, these studies are often the only opportunity
for researchers and physicians to address significant knowledge gaps and obtain a robust
understanding of the disease and patient experience.

Engaging in a Natural History Study offers numerous benefits to the community, such as:
* Raising awareness in medical, academic and pharmaceutical sectors
* Empowering rare disease patient communities with knowledge and support for advocating better
  healthcare policies and support services
* Enhancing patient care with improved insights into disease progression, allowing for more
  personalized treatment plans and potentially earlier detection of complications
* Contributing to advancements in healthcare

How do Natural History Studies help inform and design clinical trials?

These studies provide various avenues to help inform and design clinical trials, such as:
* Highlighting areas of unmet medical need
* Understanding characteristics of the patient population to define a treatment benefit from a
  patient’s perspective.
* Describing disease progression, enabling the identification of clinical outcome measures and
  biomarkers
* Provide patient-centric data for health authorities such as the FDA, and other public health
  institutions to use in their review processes of investigational treatments.

# DNA Is No Longer Destiny

Seeking gene therapy cures that correct rare and devastating diseases at their root cause. Cures
that represent freedom – freedom for patients and their loved ones to fully live in a world without
the burden of genetic disease. A world where DNA is not destiny and genetic disease is history.

[ Download our Corporate Presentation ][126]

for $180 Million][127]

## Mission, Vision & Values

Our mission is to seek gene therapy cures for patients with devastating rare diseases through the
most innovative science and platforms to fulfill the promise of gene therapy for the betterment of
our industry, science and humanity.

### Trust

+
Trust is given and trust is earned – it’s a balance. The word “trust” comes from the
“Proto-Indo-European word “deru” which means “to be firm, solid, steadfast.” Trust is the ground and
foundation for everything we do.

### Generosity

+
Being generous means following up, sharing our best ideas, forgiving ourselves and others, asking
who needs us, treating our word as gold, taking time to truly see others, and so many other things.
The word “generous” has the same root as the word “gene” – which means “to beget.” Genes thrive on
the generosity of others. What more is there to say?

### Curiosity

+
The wonder of a child staring up at the night sky. Humility, selflessness. No single one of us can
do this job alone and it is ok to ask for help. Curiosity is derived from the Latin word, “cura”
which gave birth to the word “care” as well as “cure.” Generosity is to curiosity what gene is to
cure.

### Elevate

+
Derived from the Latin word “levis,” which means “light” as opposed to heavy. How can we bring
trust, generosity and curiosity to elevate ourselves, each other, the pipeline and ultimately the
life experience of patients and their families?

**Joint Statement on Crisis in Ukraine**
The American Society of Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT), European Society for Blood
Marrow Transplantation (EBMT), and Worldwide Network for Blood Marrow Transplantation (WBMT) firmly
condemn the war started by Russian military forces in Ukraine. In particular, ASTCT, EBMT, and WBMT
request that peace negotiations prioritize the needs of the most vulnerable Ukrainian people.
Casualties among innocent civilians increase by the minute, including children. Patients with severe
conditions, such as those with cancer or undergoing life-saving transplants, are currently affected
by lack of medications and medical supplies, limited ability to travel to hospitals, lack of
adequate nutrition. Healthcare providers and hospital staff in Kyiv remain in their hospitals to
treat the patients in shelters, while bombs continue to hit the city.

Read the full letter [here][62].

Bruce Levine is a pioneer in cancer Immunotherapy and together with Carl June at UPENN/PENNMEDICINE
in Philadelphia performed the first CAR-T cell therapies in patients with CLL in 2011. This was
possible only after many years of experimental work, persistence and belief in a unique and exciting
therapy. He describes this journey as follow “In the 1990s and early 2000s, it was seen as something
boutique of ‘isn’t that quaint,’ and ‘interesting, but it’s never going to work.’ This idea of
redirecting T cells or immune cells was groundbreaking. NIH grant reviewers saw it as a totally
different paradigm than they were used to, and many comments were not kind. Since these early steps,
CAR-T cells targeting CD19 and BCMA have received regulatory approvals around the world in ALL, CLL
and NHL after relapse.  Many other CAR T therapies, including for solid tumors, are in development.
He has published several groundbreaking publications, is past-president of ISCT and was awarded to
many prestigious prizes, the last one just a months ago.
Dietger Niederwieser conducted an interview with Bruce on the history of CAR-T cells.
Recently he has partnered with an internationally acclaimed Irish country music artist **Mags
McCarthy** , who has released her most heartfelt and powerful single yet, **“Ring That Bell”**. In
an unexpected and moving collaboration, Mags has partnered with world-renowned scientist **Dr. Bruce
Levine** to co-write a song that gives voice to cancer warriors and celebrates breakthroughs in
treatment that are changing lives.

“Ring That Bell” tells the emotional story of a cancer patient facing relapse and the fierce
advocacy, support, and groundbreaking science that offer new hope. At its heart is the powerful
symbolism of ringing the bell—a tradition in many cancer centers marking key milestones like the end
of treatment, good news, or moments of gratitude and encouragement.  The music video is
here: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dkOrbjMz3zQ][63]. An exciting production for physicians,
nurses and patients.

[Watch the Interview][64]

**Joint Statement on Crisis in Ukraine**
The American Society of Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT), European Society for Blood
Marrow Transplantation (EBMT), and Worldwide Network for Blood Marrow Transplantation (WBMT) firmly
condemn the war started by Russian military forces in Ukraine. In particular, ASTCT, EBMT, and WBMT
request that peace negotiations prioritize the needs of the most vulnerable Ukrainian people.
Casualties among innocent civilians increase by the minute, including children. Patients with severe
conditions, such as those with cancer or undergoing life-saving transplants, are currently affected
by lack of medications and medical supplies, limited ability to travel to hospitals, lack of
adequate nutrition. Healthcare providers and hospital staff in Kyiv remain in their hospitals to
treat the patients in shelters, while bombs continue to hit the city.

Read the full letter [here][62].

Bruce Levine is a pioneer in cancer Immunotherapy and together with Carl June at UPENN/PENNMEDICINE
in Philadelphia performed the first CAR-T cell therapies in patients with CLL in 2011. This was
possible only after many years of experimental work, persistence and belief in a unique and exciting
therapy. He describes this journey as follow “In the 1990s and early 2000s, it was seen as something
boutique of ‘isn’t that quaint,’ and ‘interesting, but it’s never going to work.’ This idea of
redirecting T cells or immune cells was groundbreaking. NIH grant reviewers saw it as a totally
different paradigm than they were used to, and many comments were not kind. Since these early steps,
CAR-T cells targeting CD19 and BCMA have received regulatory approvals around the world in ALL, CLL
and NHL after relapse.  Many other CAR T therapies, including for solid tumors, are in development.
He has published several groundbreaking publications, is past-president of ISCT and was awarded to
many prestigious prizes, the last one just a months ago.
Dietger Niederwieser conducted an interview with Bruce on the history of CAR-T cells.
Recently he has partnered with an internationally acclaimed Irish country music artist **Mags
McCarthy** , who has released her most heartfelt and powerful single yet, **“Ring That Bell”**. In
an unexpected and moving collaboration, Mags has partnered with world-renowned scientist **Dr. Bruce
Levine** to co-write a song that gives voice to cancer warriors and celebrates breakthroughs in
treatment that are changing lives.

“Ring That Bell” tells the emotional story of a cancer patient facing relapse and the fierce
advocacy, support, and groundbreaking science that offer new hope. At its heart is the powerful
symbolism of ringing the bell—a tradition in many cancer centers marking key milestones like the end
of treatment, good news, or moments of gratitude and encouragement.  The music video is
here: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dkOrbjMz3zQ][63]. An exciting production for physicians,
nurses and patients.

[Watch the Interview][64]

# ** BEST HOSPITAL GROUP IN GHAZIABAD AND DELHI NCR**

Yashoda Healthcare (also Yashoda Group of Hospitals) is a multi-speciality chain of hospitals
located in Ghaziabad and Delhi NCR. We have been operating in the quaternary sector for more than 30
years. An 800+ bedded chain of hospitals, our group comprises of Yashoda Hospital & Research Centre,
a multi-speciality hospital located in Nehru Nagar, Ghaziabad with good metro connectivity. In
operation since 1990, it has catered to lakhs of patients at an affordable cost. Yashoda
Superspeciality Hospital & Cancer Institutes located at Sanjay Nagar, Ghaziabad is reputed to be one
of the best cancer-dedicated hospitals in the country with world-class infrastructure and ex-army
oncologists. Yashoda Super Speciality Hospitals at Vasundhara caters straight to the people of
Delhi, who now have the privilege to obtain world-class treatment at affordable prices. All three
hospitals are NABH/NABL accredited, having successfully completed NABH Accreditation Stand

# ** BEST HOSPITAL GROUP IN GHAZIABAD AND DELHI NCR**

Yashoda Healthcare (also Yashoda Group of Hospitals) is a multi-speciality chain of hospitals
located in Ghaziabad and Delhi NCR. We have been operating in the quaternary sector for more than 30
years. An 800+ bedded chain of hospitals, our group comprises of Yashoda Hospital & Research Centre,
a multi-speciality hospital located in Nehru Nagar, Ghaziabad with good metro connectivity. In
operation since 1990, it has catered to lakhs of patients at an affordable cost. Yashoda
Superspeciality Hospital & Cancer Institutes located at Sanjay Nagar, Ghaziabad is reputed to be one
of the best cancer-dedicated hospitals in the country with world-class infrastructure and ex-army
oncologists. Yashoda Super Speciality Hospitals at Vasundhara caters straight to the people of
Delhi, who now have the privilege to obtain world-class treatment at affordable prices. All three
hospitals are NABH/NABL accredited, having successfully completed NABH Accreditation Stand

## # **Herzlich Willkommen…**

… beim Zentralen Knochenmarkspender-Register Deutschland (ZKRD), der zentralen Koordinationsstelle
für die Knochenmarkspendersuche gemäß §65f des fünften Sozialgesetzbuchs. Als Knotenpunkt zwischen
Transplantationszentren, Sucheinheiten, Spenderdateien und anderen Spenderregistern auf der ganzen
Welt koordiniert das ZKRD das Zusammenwirken aller Beteiligten von der Suche nach geeigneten
Spendern bis hin zum Transport der gespendeten Zellen.

### Ziel…

… und Motto unseres Registers ist:** „Schneller zum am besten geeigneten Spender für alle Patienten
weltweit!“** Effizient und schnell setzt sich das ZKRD gemeinsam mit seinen Partnern für Patienten
ein, die an Leukämie oder einer anderen Erkrankung des blutbildenden Systems leiden und eine
Stammzellspende benötigen. Für 9 von 10 Patienten in Deutschland wird meist innerhalb weniger Wochen
ein geeigneter Spender gefunden.

### **Herzstück…**

… ist das im ZKRD entwickelte Matching-Programm OptiMatch®, das für jeden einzelnen Patienten
mögliche, passende Spender ermittelt. In Deutschland kann das ZKRD dabei auf eine Datenbank
zugreifen, die nicht nur die Daten der in 26 Spenderdateien registrierten Spendern enthält, sondern
auch die Mehrzahl aller international registrierten Spender.

### **Weltweit…**

… sucht das ZKRD für seine Patienten nach potentiell passenden Spendern und beantwortet Suchanfragen
für Patienten aus dem Ausland. Bei knapp 40 % der weltweiten nicht verwandten
Blutstammzelltransplantationen sind freiwillige Spender aus Deutschland beteiligt.

### **Services…**

… von A wie Aufträge und Abrechnung über K wie Koordination bis zu T wie Transport und Z wie
Zollabfertigung machen uns zu einem kompetenten Partner mit viel Know-how in der Suche nach dem am
besten geeigneten Spender für alle Patienten weltweit.

Auf unserer Homepage finden Sie alle relevanten Informationen rund um die Themen Stammzellspende und
Spendersuche. Sollten Sie Fragen haben, nutzen Sie gerne unser [Kontaktformular][28].

… ist das im ZKRD entwickelte Matching-Programm OptiMatch®, das für jeden einzelnen Patienten
mögliche, passende Spender ermittelt. In Deutschland kann das ZKRD dabei auf eine Datenbank
zugreifen, die nicht nur die Daten der in 26 Spenderdateien registrierten Spendern enthält, sondern
auch die Mehrzahl aller international registrierten Spender.

### **Weltweit…**

… sucht das ZKRD für seine Patienten nach potentiell passenden Spendern und beantwortet Suchanfragen
für Patienten aus dem Ausland. Bei knapp 40 % der weltweiten nicht verwandten
Blutstammzelltransplantationen sind freiwillige Spender aus Deutschland beteiligt.

### **Services…**

… von A wie Aufträge und Abrechnung über K wie Koordination bis zu T wie Transport und Z wie
Zollabfertigung machen uns zu einem kompetenten Partner mit viel Know-how in der Suche nach dem am
besten geeigneten Spender für alle Patienten weltweit.

Auf unserer Homepage finden Sie alle relevanten Informationen rund um die Themen Stammzellspende und
Spendersuche. Sollten Sie Fragen haben, nutzen Sie gerne unser [Kontaktformular][28].

## Zydus Hospital - Ahmedabad

Zydus Hospital has always strived to create milestones of recovery stories since inception. We have
been restoring hope and health while being recognized for sheer dedication, precision, excellence,
and selfless service. Whether it is about our sound infrastructure, patient-centric approach, team
of experts, medical facilities, cutting-edge technology, transparency or emergency services, we have
constantly received words of appreciation. The hospital is an initiative by the Zydus Group.

We are a 550 bed super-specialty medical institution spanning 16 floors and two basement floors. We
offer all major medical specialties, super & sub-specialties, investigations & diagnostic
facilities, and rehabilitation & physiotherapy care under one roof. Hospital is designed considering
the need for open spaces within the hospital complex and the permeation of sunlight throughout the
day to ensure a more amicable environment to our patients and caregivers.

Our unwavering commitment is to prioritize patients above all else. Our stringent policy of
appointing only full-time doctors and experienced medical staff reflect our commitment to ensuring
dedicated and compassionate services.

[Hospital Image]

## Zydus Cancer Hospital

Zydus Cancer Hospital rises as a fortress of advanced cancer care and unwavering hope against this
challenging condition. More than just a cancer hospital in Ahmedabad, this is where the brilliant
minds with cutting-edge technologies come together to help you fight this tough battle. Our team of
experts also includes renowned Padmashree-awardees and leading talent from across the nation.

Recognized as the best cancer hospital in Ahmedabad, Zydus Cancer Hospital offers the 32-Slice PET
CT scan, Gamma Camera SPECT, and houses the largest Bone Marrow Transplant unit in Gujarat, and
more. Focusing on homely patient care, Zydus Cancer Hospital provides various treatment procedures
for all types of cancer. The state-of-the-art infrastructure has 3D Mammography with HD
Tomosynthesis for Breast Cancer treatments, Radionuclide therapies, Radiation therapy including TBI
& ABC therapy, Scarless Head & Neck cancer surgeries, and Tumor removal procedures.

The reconstruction team at Zydus Cancer Hospital has performed some of the most complex surgeries
and has given a fresh ray of hope to countless patients. The team also specialises in
Reconstruction, Re-implantation, and Cosmetic surgery. On the other hand, Zydus Cancer Hospital also
has renowned surgeons who specialise in Robotic procedures for GI, Thoracic, Urology, and Head &
Neck cancer surgeries. Our Gynec-onco team has also treated a large number of patients with critical
conditions.

Zydus Cancer Hospital is led by a remarkable team of specialists who are pioneers in their domains
and are trusted with the most complex cases not only in the state but across the country.

[Hospital Image]

## Zydus Hospital - Vadodara

Zydus Multispeciality and Cancer Hospital in Vadodara is committed to delivering top-notch medical
services across the healthcare industry. We provide end-to-end comprehensive care, ensuring patients
receive everything they require under one roof

Our dedicated team of full-time medical practitioners and expert nursing staff upholds the highest
standards of honesty and transparency in all our services. Zydus, Vadodara, a 300-bed
multi-specialty hospital with a cancer hospital spread across 4 lakh sq. ft, is one of the biggest
hospitals in Vadodara. It brings a unique combination of the best infrastructure with renowned
healthcare experts, along with highly skilled medical staff, making Zydus Vadodara one of the best
hospitals in the city. The hospital specializes in Heart Care, Cancer Care, Kidney Care, Orthopedic
Care, and Neuro Care, always prioritizing patient safety and delivering the finest medical care with
a patient-centric approach.

[Hospital Image]

## Zydus Hospital - Anand

Zydus Hospital, Anand, Gujarat, has earned numerous accolades and has become the leading advanced
tertiary care multi-specialty hospital. Since its inception in 2012, we have boasted a team of
well-known doctors and medical staff who promise to deliver top-quality healthcare services.
Offering a wide range of surgeries across departments, Zydus has become a trusted name for both
complex surgeries and routine healthcare needs in Anand.

Zydus Anand offers the best Cardiac Care, Neuro Care, Gastro and Kidney Care. Zydus Anand also
treats patients across specialties such as Orthopedics and Liver, and is widely known for our
Bariatric Care. Ranked as one of the best hospitals in Anand, Zydus is renowned for its
comprehensive approach and pioneering clinical excellence. Our highly skilled medical staff, along
with modern infrastructure and advanced technologies, promises to deliver top-quality healthcare
services to all our patients. From emergency care to elective surgeries, complex interventions to
everyday wellness, Zydus Hospital, Anand, provides holistic healthcare under one roof.

#### LIVER TRANSPLANT

Zydus is ranked among the best liver hospitals, with a transplant program supported by a
multidisciplinary team of over 20 specialists, including hepatobiliary and liver transplant
surgeons, critical care experts, hepatologists, and transplant anesthesiologists. Our track record
includes complex living donor and cadaveric liver transplants, performed with precision and
supported by stringent infection control, hemodynamic monitoring, and long-term graft function
protocols.

#### KIDNEY TRANSPLANT

As the best kidney hospital in Ahmedabad, our nephrology and urology teams bring years of
transplant-specific expertise. From ABO-incompatible to sensitized recipient protocols, our
specialists manage every stage of donor selection, intraoperative care, immunosuppression planning,
and long-term nephroprotective strategies, with rigorous clinical oversight and individualized
follow-up pathways.

#### BONE MARROW TRANSPLANT

Here, the bone marrow transplant unit is helmed by hematologists with deep experience in high-risk
malignancies, aplastic anemia, and rare blood disorders. As the best cancer hospital in Ahmedabad,
we offer autologous, allogeneic, and matched unrelated donor transplants with dedicated
HEPA-filtered BMT suites, 24x7 hematology-intensivist coverage, and advanced GVHD prophylaxis and
management protocols.

Zydus stands as a leading heart specialist hospital in Ahmedabad, offering a state-of-the-art heart
transplant program backed by advanced cardiac imaging, ECMO-supported bridging, and a dedicated
transplant ICU. Our surgical teams and heart failure specialists work collaboratively to manage both
pre-transplant optimization and long-term cardiac rehabilitation, ensuring continuity of care from
diagnosis through recovery.

## Zydus Hospital - Ahmedabad

Zydus Hospital has always strived to create milestones of recovery stories since inception. We have
been restoring hope and health while being recognized for sheer dedication, precision, excellence,
and selfless service. Whether it is about our sound infrastructure, patient-centric approach, team
of experts, medical facilities, cutting-edge technology, transparency or emergency services, we have
constantly received words of appreciation. The hospital is an initiative by the Zydus Group.

We are a 550 bed super-specialty medical institution spanning 16 floors and two basement floors. We
offer all major medical specialties, super & sub-specialties, investigations & diagnostic
facilities, and rehabilitation & physiotherapy care under one roof. Hospital is designed considering
the need for open spaces within the hospital complex and the permeation of sunlight throughout the
day to ensure a more amicable environment to our patients and caregivers.

Our unwavering commitment is to prioritize patients above all else. Our stringent policy of
appointing only full-time doctors and experienced medical staff reflect our commitment to ensuring
dedicated and compassionate services.

[Hospital Image]

## Zydus Cancer Hospital

Zydus Cancer Hospital rises as a fortress of advanced cancer care and unwavering hope against this
challenging condition. More than just a cancer hospital in Ahmedabad, this is where the brilliant
minds with cutting-edge technologies come together to help you fight this tough battle. Our team of
experts also includes renowned Padmashree-awardees and leading talent from across the nation.

Recognized as the best cancer hospital in Ahmedabad, Zydus Cancer Hospital offers the 32-Slice PET
CT scan, Gamma Camera SPECT, and houses the largest Bone Marrow Transplant unit in Gujarat, and
more. Focusing on homely patient care, Zydus Cancer Hospital provides various treatment procedures
for all types of cancer. The state-of-the-art infrastructure has 3D Mammography with HD
Tomosynthesis for Breast Cancer treatments, Radionuclide therapies, Radiation therapy including TBI
& ABC therapy, Scarless Head & Neck cancer surgeries, and Tumor removal procedures.

The reconstruction team at Zydus Cancer Hospital has performed some of the most complex surgeries
and has given a fresh ray of hope to countless patients. The team also specialises in
Reconstruction, Re-implantation, and Cosmetic surgery. On the other hand, Zydus Cancer Hospital also
has renowned surgeons who specialise in Robotic procedures for GI, Thoracic, Urology, and Head &
Neck cancer surgeries. Our Gynec-onco team has also treated a large number of patients with critical
conditions.

Zydus Cancer Hospital is led by a remarkable team of specialists who are pioneers in their domains
and are trusted with the most complex cases not only in the state but across the country.

[Hospital Image]

## Zydus Hospital - Vadodara

Zydus Multispeciality and Cancer Hospital in Vadodara is committed to delivering top-notch medical
services across the healthcare industry. We provide end-to-end comprehensive care, ensuring patients
receive everything they require under one roof

Our dedicated team of full-time medical practitioners and expert nursing staff upholds the highest
standards of honesty and transparency in all our services. Zydus, Vadodara, a 300-bed
multi-specialty hospital with a cancer hospital spread across 4 lakh sq. ft, is one of the biggest
hospitals in Vadodara. It brings a unique combination of the best infrastructure with renowned
healthcare experts, along with highly skilled medical staff, making Zydus Vadodara one of the best
hospitals in the city. The hospital specializes in Heart Care, Cancer Care, Kidney Care, Orthopedic
Care, and Neuro Care, always prioritizing patient safety and delivering the finest medical care with
a patient-centric approach.

[Hospital Image]

## Zydus Hospital - Anand

Zydus Hospital, Anand, Gujarat, has earned numerous accolades and has become the leading advanced
tertiary care multi-specialty hospital. Since its inception in 2012, we have boasted a team of
well-known doctors and medical staff who promise to deliver top-quality healthcare services.
Offering a wide range of surgeries across departments, Zydus has become a trusted name for both
complex surgeries and routine healthcare needs in Anand.

Zydus Anand offers the best Cardiac Care, Neuro Care, Gastro and Kidney Care. Zydus Anand also
treats patients across specialties such as Orthopedics and Liver, and is widely known for our
Bariatric Care. Ranked as one of the best hospitals in Anand, Zydus is renowned for its
comprehensive approach and pioneering clinical excellence. Our highly skilled medical staff, along
with modern infrastructure and advanced technologies, promises to deliver top-quality healthcare
services to all our patients. From emergency care to elective surgeries, complex interventions to
everyday wellness, Zydus Hospital, Anand, provides holistic healthcare under one roof.

#### LIVER TRANSPLANT

Zydus is ranked among the best liver hospitals, with a transplant program supported by a
multidisciplinary team of over 20 specialists, including hepatobiliary and liver transplant
surgeons, critical care experts, hepatologists, and transplant anesthesiologists. Our track record
includes complex living donor and cadaveric liver transplants, performed with precision and
supported by stringent infection control, hemodynamic monitoring, and long-term graft function
protocols.

#### KIDNEY TRANSPLANT

As the best kidney hospital in Ahmedabad, our nephrology and urology teams bring years of
transplant-specific expertise. From ABO-incompatible to sensitized recipient protocols, our
specialists manage every stage of donor selection, intraoperative care, immunosuppression planning,
and long-term nephroprotective strategies, with rigorous clinical oversight and individualized
follow-up pathways.

#### BONE MARROW TRANSPLANT

Here, the bone marrow transplant unit is helmed by hematologists with deep experience in high-risk
malignancies, aplastic anemia, and rare blood disorders. As the best cancer hospital in Ahmedabad,
we offer autologous, allogeneic, and matched unrelated donor transplants with dedicated
HEPA-filtered BMT suites, 24x7 hematology-intensivist coverage, and advanced GVHD prophylaxis and
management protocols.

#### HEART TRANSPLANT

Zydus stands as a leading heart specialist hospital in Ahmedabad, offering a state-of-the-art heart
transplant program backed by advanced cardiac imaging, ECMO-supported bridging, and a dedicated
transplant ICU. Our surgical teams and heart failure specialists work collaboratively to manage both
pre-transplant optimization and long-term cardiac rehabilitation, ensuring continuity of care from
diagnosis through recovery.
